record.paper_title: Open Questions in Charm Decays Deserving an Answer
record.original_question: What are the absolute branching ratios of D_s, Lambda_c, and Xi_c decays to precision far better than the current tens-of-percent level, so that charm-hadron final states can be used reliably as normalization inputs in beauty-decay measurements and in determinations of |V(cb)|?

evidence.quote: Nothing is known in this respect about Ξc and precious little about Λc decays. Reviewing events over the last two years I feel little confident that the absolute branching ratios for Ds decays are known to better than 30% – if even that.

The uncertainties in the charm branching ratios are emerging as the limiting factor in determining the branching ratios of beauty decays such as B → lνD(∗) , Bs → lνD(∗) s and Λb → lνΛc, with obvious consequences for extracting a numerical value for |V (cb)|.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
In the Standard Model of particle physics, the charmed hadrons $D_s^+$ (a meson with quark content $c ar s$), $\Lambda_c^+$ (a baryon with content $udc$), and $\Xi_c$ (baryons with content $usc$ or $dsc$) decay weakly via the charm quark transition $c	o s$ (or $c	o d$). For each ground-state charmed hadron $H_c\in\{D_s^+,\Lambda_c^+,\Xi_c^0,\Xi_c^+\}$, and for each exclusive hadronic decay mode $H_c	o f$ (e.g., $D_s^+	o\phi\pi^+$, $\Lambda_c^+	o pK^-\pi^+$, $\Xi_c^+	o\Xi^-\pi^+\pi^+$), determine the absolute branching fraction $\mathcal{B}(H_c	o f)$, defined as the partial decay width to $f$ divided by the total width of $H_c$, to a fractional precision substantially better than the order of tens of percent that was available historically. The required precision is that needed so that these branching fractions serve as reliable normalization inputs in measurements of beauty-hadron semileptonic decays $B	o\ell
u D^{(*)}$, $B_s	o\ell
u D_s^{(*)}$, and $\Lambda_b	o\ell
u\Lambda_c$ used in the extraction of the Cabibbo–Kobayashi–Maskawa matrix element $|V_{cb}|$.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem has been substantially advanced since the original question. BESIII, CLEO-c, Belle, and LHCb have measured absolute branching fractions of $D_s^+$ and $\Lambda_c^+$ decays at the few-percent level: e.g., BESIII determined $\mathcal{B}(\Lambda_c^+\to pK^-\pi^+)=(6.61\pm 0.11\pm 0.12)\%$, a 2–3-fold precision improvement. Comparable progress has been made for many $D_s^+$ modes. For $\Xi_c^{0,+}$, absolute branching fractions have only recently begun to be measured (e.g., Belle's $\Xi_c^+\to\Xi^-\pi^+\pi^+$ and $\Xi_c^0\to\Xi^-\pi^+$) and remain less precise. Thus the problem is partially solved.

status_evidence.title: Measurements of the absolute branching fractions of the Λc+ hadronic decays
status_evidence.snippet: Λc+ → pK-π+ branching fraction determined to (6.61±0.11±0.12)%, precision improved by a factor of 2 to 3.
status_evidence.claim: Absolute branching fractions of Λc+ hadronic decays have been measured by BESIII with substantially improved precision.

status_evidence.title: Improved measurement of absolute branching fraction of the inclusive decay Λc+→K0S X
status_evidence.snippet: Improved measurement of absolute inclusive branching fraction of Λc+ → K0_S X at BESIII.
status_evidence.claim: Continued precision improvements of Λc+ absolute branching fractions are ongoing as of 2025.
